title.en: BERT vs GPT: Pre-training & Fine-tuning Giants

description.en: Understand the key differences between BERT (bidirectional encoder) and GPT (autoregressive decoder), their pre-training objectives, and how to fine-tune them.
description.ta: BERT (bidirectional encoder) மற்றும் GPT (autoregressive decoder) இடையேயான முக்கிய வேறுபாடுகள், அவற்றின் முன்-பயிற்சி நோக்கங்கள், நுண்-சரிப்படுத்தும் முறைகளைப் புரிந்துகொள்ளுங்கள்.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Two Prodigies

Vaathiyaar introduces two brilliant students. "BERT reads the whole sentence at once — fill in the blanks. GPT reads left to right — predict the next word. Both learned from billions of words. Now you can teach them your specific task with just a little data."

### BERT: Bidirectional Encoder

```python
import torch
from torch import nn

# Simulating BERT-like masked language model
class MiniMLM(nn.Module):
    """Masked Language Model (BERT-style pre-training)"""
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, d_model=256, num_heads=8, num_layers=6):
        super().__init__()
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model, nhead=num_heads, dim_feedforward=1024,
            batch_first=True, dropout=0.1
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=num_layers)
        self.mlm_head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.embedding(x)
        x = self.encoder(x)
        return self.mlm_head(x)

# Pre-training: mask 15% of tokens, predict them
def mask_tokens(input_ids, vocab_size, mask_token_id, mask_prob=0.15):
    labels = input_ids.clone()
    mask = torch.rand(input_ids.shape) < mask_prob
    input_ids[mask] = mask_token_id  # replace with [MASK]
    labels[~mask] = -100             # only compute loss on masked tokens
    return input_ids, labels
```

### GPT: Autoregressive Decoder

```python
class MiniGPT(nn.Module):
    """Causal Language Model (GPT-style)"""
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, d_model=256, num_heads=8, num_layers=6, max_len=512):
        super().__init__()
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.pos_embedding = nn.Embedding(max_len, d_model)
        decoder_layer = nn.TransformerDecoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model, nhead=num_heads, dim_feedforward=1024,
            batch_first=True, dropout=0.1
        )
        self.decoder = nn.TransformerDecoder(decoder_layer, num_layers=num_layers)
        self.lm_head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        seq_len = x.size(1)
        positions = torch.arange(seq_len, device=x.device).unsqueeze(0)
        x = self.embedding(x) + self.pos_embedding(positions)
        # Causal mask: can only attend to past
        mask = nn.Transformer.generate_square_subsequent_mask(seq_len).to(x.device)
        memory = torch.zeros_like(x)  # no encoder for decoder-only
        x = self.decoder(x, memory, tgt_mask=mask)
        return self.lm_head(x)
```

### Fine-tuning for Classification

```python
class BERTClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, pretrained_bert, num_classes):
        super().__init__()
        self.bert = pretrained_bert
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(256, num_classes)  # d_model=256
    
    def forward(self, x):
        encoded = self.bert.encoder(self.bert.embedding(x))
        cls_token = encoded[:, 0, :]  # [CLS] token representation
        return self.classifier(cls_token)
```

> **BERT:** Great for understanding (classification, NER, Q&A). **GPT:** Great for generation (text, code, chat).
story_variants.ta:
## வாத்தியாரின் இரண்டு மேதைகள்

வாத்தியார் இரண்டு அறிவாளி மாணவர்களை அறிமுகப்படுத்துகிறார். "BERT முழு வாக்கியத்தையும் ஒரே நேரத்தில் படிக்கிறது — வெற்றிடங்களை நிரப்புங்கள். GPT இடமிருந்து வலமாக படிக்கிறது — அடுத்த வார்த்தையை கணிக்கவும். இரண்டும் கோடிக்கணக்கான வார்த்தைகளிலிருந்து கற்றன."

steps.line: # BERT: mask 15% of tokens, predict them

explanation.en: BERT pre-training: randomly mask words, model predicts them using bidirectional context
Replace 15% of tokens with [MASK]. Model must use surrounding context to predict original word
Set non-masked positions to -100 (ignored by CrossEntropyLoss). Only train on masked tokens
BERT uses encoder (bidirectional attention — each token sees all other tokens)
GPT pre-training: predict the next token given all previous tokens. Autoregressive.
Causal mask: token at position i can only attend to positions 0..i (not future)
GPT uses decoder with causal masking — each token only sees past tokens
BERT fine-tuning: use [CLS] token (position 0) as the sentence representation
Add a small classification head on top of the pre-trained model
Modern LLMs scale from millions to hundreds of billions of parameters

instruction.en: PyTorch cannot run in this sandbox, so this is the numpy version of what PyTorch does under the hood. Explore the two big ideas behind BERT and GPT. 1) `attention_mask(n, causal)`: GPT is causal, so each token may only see itself and earlier tokens (a lower-triangular n x n matrix of 1s); BERT is bidirectional (all 1s). 2) `mask_tokens(tokens, positions, mask_token="[MASK]")` returns a NEW list with those positions replaced by the mask token, plus a dict {position: original word} - the labels for masked-language-model training. 3) `predict_masked(tokens, pos, bigrams)` predicts the masked word BERT-style, using both neighbours: for every word that appears in `bigrams`, score = bigrams[(left, word)] + bigrams[(word, right)] (a missing neighbour or pair counts 0); return the best word (alphabetically first on ties).
instruction.ta: இந்த sandbox-ல் PyTorch இயங்காது, எனவே இது PyTorch உள்ளே செய்வதன் numpy பதிப்பு. BERT, GPT பின்னால் உள்ள இரண்டு பெரிய கருத்துகளை ஆராயுங்கள். 1) `attention_mask(n, causal)`: GPT causal, எனவே ஒவ்வொரு token-உம் தன்னையும் முந்தைய tokens-ஐயும் மட்டுமே பார்க்க முடியும் (1-களால் ஆன lower-triangular n x n matrix); BERT bidirectional (அனைத்தும் 1). 2) `mask_tokens(tokens, positions, mask_token="[MASK]")` அந்த நிலைகளை mask token-ஆல் மாற்றிய ஒரு புதிய list-ஐயும், {position: மூலச் சொல்} dict-ஐயும் திருப்புகிறது - masked language model பயிற்சிக்கான labels. 3) `predict_masked(tokens, pos, bigrams)` BERT போல இரு பக்க அண்டைச் சொற்களையும் பயன்படுத்தி mask செய்யப்பட்ட சொல்லைக் கணிக்கிறது: `bigrams`-ல் வரும் ஒவ்வொரு சொல்லுக்கும் score = bigrams[(left, word)] + bigrams[(word, right)] (அண்டைச் சொல் அல்லது ஜோடி இல்லையெனில் 0); சிறந்த சொல்லைத் திருப்புங்கள் (சமநிலையில் அகர வரிசைப்படி முதலாவது).

practice_challenges.test_code:
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter
_c = attention_mask(3, causal=True)
assert _c is not None and np.array_equal(_c, [[1, 0, 0], [1, 1, 0], [1, 1, 1]]), "the causal (GPT) mask must be lower-triangular ones"
assert np.array_equal(attention_mask(3, causal=False), np.ones((3, 3))), "the bidirectional (BERT) mask must be all ones"
_toks = ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
_r = mask_tokens(_toks, [1, 3])
assert isinstance(_r, tuple) and len(_r) == 2, "mask_tokens must return (masked_tokens, labels)"
assert list(_r[0]) == ["a", "[MASK]", "c", "[MASK]"] and _r[1] == {1: "b", 3: "d"}, "mask the given positions and remember the originals as labels"
assert _toks == ["a", "b", "c", "d"], "mask_tokens must not change the original list"
assert list(mask_tokens(_toks, [0], mask_token="<m>")[0])[0] == "<m>", "use the mask_token argument"
_bg = Counter({("a", "x"): 2, ("a", "y"): 1, ("y", "b"): 3})
assert predict_masked(["a", "[MASK]", "b"], 1, _bg) == "y", "BERT uses BOTH sides: 'y' scores 1 + 3 = 4 and beats 'x' (2 + 0)"
assert predict_masked(["a", "[MASK]"], 1, _bg) == "x", "with no right neighbour, only the left pair counts"
assert predict_masked(["[MASK]", "b"], 0, _bg) == "y", "with no left neighbour, only the right pair counts"
assert predict_masked(["q", "[MASK]", "q"], 1, Counter({("m", "n"): 1})) == "m", "on a tie, return the alphabetically first word"
print("All BERT/GPT tests passed!")

under_the_hood.summary: BERT and GPT use the same transformer blocks but differ in what each token may look at and what it must predict: BERT sees the whole sentence and fills in masked tokens, GPT sees only earlier tokens and predicts the next one at every position.

steps.title: The attention mask is the key difference
steps.body: For a 4-token input, BERT's mask lets every token attend to all 4. GPT's causal mask is lower-triangular: token 1 sees only itself, token 4 sees tokens 1 to 4. This one matrix decides whether a model reads in both directions or strictly left to right.

props.caption: BERT: every token may attend to every token (1 = allowed)

steps.title: GPT's causal mask
steps.body: The same 4 tokens under GPT's mask: row i has 1s only up to column i. Because no position can see what comes after it, the model can be trained to predict token i + 1 from row i without cheating, and later generate text one token at a time.

steps.title: BERT pre-training: masked language modelling
steps.body: BERT picks 15% of token positions. Of those, 80% become [MASK], 10% a random token and 10% stay unchanged, so the model cannot rely on seeing [MASK]. The loss is computed only at the chosen positions: 'The [MASK] sat on the mat' should predict 'cat' using words on both sides.

steps.title: GPT pre-training: next token everywhere
steps.body: GPT shifts the sequence by one: inputs 'The cat sat on', targets 'cat sat on the'. Every position contributes to the loss, so each sentence gives as many training signals as it has tokens. The same objective then drives generation: predict, append, repeat.

left.label: BERT objective
left.code:
loss on ~15% masked positions
uses left and right context

right.label: GPT objective
right.code:
loss on every position
uses left context only

steps.title: Fine-tuning attaches a small head
steps.body: For classification, BERT's final vector at the [CLS] token goes into a new linear layer, and the whole model is trained briefly on labelled examples with a small learning rate (often around 2e-5). GPT-style models are adapted by prompting, instruction tuning or fine-tuning on example completions.

under_the_hood.takeaway: Same blocks, different mask and objective. Bidirectional masking makes BERT strong at understanding a given text; causal masking makes GPT able to write text, which is why chat models are GPT-style.
